info.title: Plexus API
info.summary: Unified gateway for LLM provider APIs with usage tracking, quotas, cooldowns, and an admin management plane.
info.description:
Plexus is a unified API gateway for LLM providers. It exposes OpenAI-, Anthropic-, and Gemini-compatible endpoints and routes requests to any backend provider, handling request/response transformation automatically.

## Surfaces

Plexus exposes three logical surfaces:

1. **Inference APIs** (`/v1/*`, `/v1beta/*`) — OpenAI-, Anthropic-, and
   Gemini-compatible endpoints that transparently fan out to configured
   upstream providers. Authenticated with a Plexus API key (see the
   [`PlexusApiKey`](#/components/securitySchemes/PlexusApiKey) security
   scheme).

2. **Management APIs** (`/v0/management/*`) — Administrative operations
   (configuration CRUD, usage analytics, debug tracing, quotas, OAuth
   onboarding, Prometheus metrics, etc.). Authenticated with the
   `x-admin-key` header. The admin header may be either the server's
   `ADMIN_KEY` (full access) or the plaintext secret of a configured
   API key (limited access, scoped to that key's own data). Endpoints
   marked with the `AdminOnly` note reject limited principals with 403.

3. **Raw Provider Proxy** (`/raw/{provider}/*`) — Relays provider-native
   HTTP traffic without model routing or payload transformation. Requires
   explicit provider and inference-key opt-in.


4. **MCP Proxy** (`/mcp/:name`) — Proxies JSON-RPC and SSE traffic to
   database-registered MCP servers. Plus unauthenticated MCP OAuth
   discovery under `/.well-known/*` and `POST /register`.


## Authentication

### Inference (`PlexusApiKey`)

A Plexus API key is accepted from any of the following, checked in order:

| Location | Example | |---|---| | `Authorization` header (Bearer) | `Authorization: Bearer sk-my-key` | | `Authorization` header (no prefix) | `Authorization: sk-my-key` (server prepends `Bearer`) | | `x-api-key` header | `x-api-key: sk-my-key` | | `x-goog-api-key` header | `x-goog-api-key: sk-my-key` | | `?key=` query parameter | `GET /v1/models?key=sk-my-key` |

Keys are matched against the `secret` field of entries in the `keys` configuration table.

### Management (`AdminKey`)

Pass the header `x-admin-key: <value>`. A successful match with `process.env.ADMIN_KEY` produces an `admin` principal. Any other value is checked against `keys[*].secret` — a match yields a `limited` principal scoped to its own key's usage/debug/error records. Limited principals are rejected (403) from endpoints documented as admin-only.

Use `GET /v0/management/auth/verify` to test a candidate admin/key credential before storing it in the dashboard.

## Dynamic key attribution

Append `:label` to a Plexus API key (e.g. `sk-abc:copilot`) to tag every resulting usage record with an `attribution` label. The label surfaces in the `UsageRecord.attribution` field and in `api_key_attribution_*` Prometheus metrics.

## Principal model

The `x-admin-key` header resolves to one of two principal types:

- **`admin`** — full access to every management endpoint. Matched when
  the header equals `process.env.ADMIN_KEY`.
- **`limited`** — scoped to the key's own usage, debug, and error
  records. Matched when the header equals a configured key's `secret`.
  Limited principals are rejected (403) from admin-only endpoints.

On `/v0/management/self/*` routes an `admin` principal can impersonate any key by passing `?keyName=<name>`.

## Header forwarding

The following client headers, when present, are forwarded to upstream providers:

- `x-app` — application identifier. Echoed into
  `plexus_metadata.clientHeaders` on the usage record (all inference
  routes).
- `session_id` — client session identifier. Forwarded as an HTTP
  header for prompt cache routing (`/v1/responses` only).
- `x-client-request-id` — client-supplied request correlation ID.
  Forwarded as an HTTP header for prompt cache routing
  (`/v1/responses` only).


## Environment variables

Key environment variables that affect runtime behaviour:

| Variable | Purpose | |---|---| | `ADMIN_KEY` | Master admin key for management endpoints. | | `DATA_DIR` | Directory for SQLite database and data files. | | `LOG_LEVEL` | Runtime log level (`error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug`, `verbose`, `silly`). | | `DEBUG` | Set to `true` to enable debug log capture at startup. | | `PLEXUS_METRICS_CACHE_TTL_MS` | TTL for the Prometheus metrics cache in milliseconds. | | `DATABASE_URL` | Connection string for PostgreSQL (omit for SQLite). | | `ENCRYPTION_KEY` | Key used to encrypt secrets at rest. |

See `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` for the full list and configuration file format.

## Public endpoints (no auth)

- `GET /health` - `GET /v1/models` - `GET /v1/openrouter/models` - `GET /v1/metadata/search` - `GET /v1/metadata/lookup` - All `/.well-known/*` MCP discovery endpoints - `POST /register` (MCP dynamic client registration)

Requests are dispatched through the transformer pipeline: the `model` field is resolved against configured aliases, the request is transformed to the target provider format, the upstream call is made, and the response is transformed back.
When an upstream provider fails, Plexus retries across alternate targets per the failover policy. Providers that return consecutive errors are placed on exponential-backoff cooldown (see the `Management — Cooldowns` tag).

tags.name: Management — OAuth
tags.description:
Per-provider OAuth onboarding sessions (pi-ai).
Sessions follow a state machine:
``` waiting → prompt ↔ manual-code → complete
           \            |
            → cancelled ←
            → failed
```
- **waiting** — session created, waiting for user to open the auth URL. - **prompt** — provider requires a user confirmation (e.g. "yes"). - **manual-code** — provider requires a manually pasted auth code
  (e.g. Codex CLI, Claude Code).
- **complete** — credentials stored, provider ready. - **failed** — authentication error. - **cancelled** — user cancelled the session.
Providers that use the callback server (`usesCallbackServer: true`) transition automatically; others require manual code paste.

tags.name: Management — Quotas (Provider)
tags.description:
Upstream provider quota checkers (`checkerId`-based).
Each checker periodically polls an upstream provider for its current quota utilisation and persists a `Meter` snapshot (one row per meter). Each meter is identified by a provider-specific `meterKey` (e.g. `balance`, `five_hour`, `daily`) rather than a fixed window-type enum. Use `GET /quotas/{checkerId}/history?meterKey=...` for historical rows, and `GET /quotas/{checkerId}` for the latest meter readings.
### Status thresholds
| Status | Utilisation | Description | |---|---|---| | `ok` | 0–75% | Healthy, plenty of quota remaining. | | `warning` | 75–90% | Approaching exhaustion. | | `critical` | 90–100% | Near exhaustion, take action soon. | | `exhausted` | 100% | Quota fully consumed, requests will fail. |

tags.name: Management — Quotas (User)
tags.description:
Per-API-key quota definitions and enforcement.
### Definition lifecycle
1. Create a quota definition with `PUT /v0/management/user-quotas/{name}` 2. Assign it to keys via `keys[*].quota` in config or `PATCH /keys/{name}` 3. The enforcement middleware checks requests against the assigned quota
### Assignment vs enforcement separation
- **Assignment**: A quota definition is linked to a key via the key's
  `quota` field or via the keys API.
- **Enforcement**: The middleware evaluates the key's usage against its
  assigned quota definition at request time. If `quota_name` is null,
  the key has no quota and is unlimited.

### Why 200 for "no quota"
`GET /v0/management/quota/status/{key}` returns 200 (not 404) even when no quota is assigned. This is intentional — the UI needs to render a "no quota" state (unlimited) rather than an error state.

tags.name: Management — Backup
tags.description:
Full database export and import for disaster recovery and migration. Two backup modes are available:
- **Config-only** (default): Exports providers, model aliases, API keys,
  user quotas, MCP servers, system settings, and OAuth credentials as a
  JSON envelope. Small and fast — covers most migration and cloning needs.
- **Full backup** (`?full=true`): Exports configuration plus all
  operational/telemetry data (usage records, debug logs, errors, cooldowns,
  performance stats, quota snapshots, responses) as a gzipped tar archive
  with per-table compressed CSV files.

Both endpoints are admin-only. Backup files contain decrypted secrets (API keys, OAuth tokens) and should be stored securely.

tags.name: MCP Proxy
tags.description:
JSON-RPC/SSE proxy for configured MCP servers plus OAuth discovery.
### Header forwarding rules
- Client `Authorization` header is **stripped** — not forwarded to
  upstream servers.
- Client `x-api-key` header is **stripped** — not forwarded. - Static `headers` from the server's config are forwarded to the
  upstream.

### Redaction
Sensitive headers are removed from requests flowing through the proxy. Only configured static headers from `mcp_servers` are used.
### Session semantics
Each proxy connection maintains a session with the upstream MCP server. Sessions are per-connection and terminate when the client disconnects or `DELETE` is called.
### OAuth discovery endpoints
The `.well-known/*` and `/register` endpoints exist solely for MCP client compatibility — they return static metadata and don't perform functional OAuth.

post.summary: OpenAI-compatible chat completion
post.description:
Drop-in replacement for `POST https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions`.
The full OpenAI request schema is accepted as-is.

## Transformer pipeline

Requests flow through:
1. `model` field resolved against configured aliases → target provider
2. Request transformed to target provider format
3. Upstream call executed
4. Response transformed back to OpenAI shape

## Routing

The `model` value is matched against configured aliases. If no alias matches,
Plexus treats it as a direct `provider/model` syntax and attempts passthrough.

## Caching

Plexus respects standard cache headers:
- `Cache-Control: no-cache` — bypasses any response caching
- `x-plexus-force-fresh` — forces a fresh upstream request

Add `:label` to your API key (e.g. `sk-abc:copilot`) to tag usage with attribution.

## Streaming

When `stream: true`, responses use Server-Sent Events (`text/event-stream`)
with `data: {...}` frames containing chat completions deltas, terminated by
`data: [DONE]`.

Forwarded client headers: `x-app` (echoed into usage `plexus_metadata.clientHeaders`),
`session_id`, `x-client-request-id` (for prompt cache routing on `/v1/responses`).

messages.content: What is the weather in Tokyo?

200.description:
A non-streamed JSON response or, when `stream: true`,
a `text/event-stream` of `data: {...}` frames terminated by
`data: [DONE]`.

schema.description: SSE frames of Chat Completions deltas.

post.summary: Anthropic-compatible messages endpoint
post.description:
Drop-in replacement for `POST https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages`.

## Anthropic-specific quirks

- **`system` top-level**: Unlike OpenAI where system messages live in the
  `messages` array, Anthropic accepts `system` as a top-level field.
- **`max_tokens` required**: Must be provided; determines maximum response length.
- **Tool use blocks**: When using tools, the response includes `tool_use` blocks
  with `input` (the tool call) and `type: tool_use`. Continue the conversation
  by submitting a `tool` role message with the tool result.

Streaming uses SSE with Anthropic event types (`message_start`, `content_block_start`,
`content_block_delta`, `message_delta`, etc.).

get.description:
Runs the management `authenticate` hook only. Used by the admin UI login
screen to confirm a credential before persisting it to local storage.

## Two response shapes

**Admin credential**: Returns `{ ok: true, role: "admin" }` — admins have
full access to all management endpoints.

**Limited credential**: Returns `{ ok: true, role: "limited", keyName, 
allowedProviders, allowedModels, quotaName, comment }` — restricted
to the configured provider/model/quotas.

The UI shows different options based on this `role` value.

## 401 conditions

- Missing `Authorization` header
- Invalid key (not found in config)
- Expired key

200.description: Credential is valid. `role` indicates the principal class.

get.description:
Returns the authenticated principal's identity and permissions.

## Two response shapes

**Admin** — Simple response with just `{ role: "admin" }`. Admins have
full access to all management endpoints.

**Limited** — Full key metadata including:
- `keyName` — The key's identifier
- `allowedProviders` — Array of provider slugs this key can use (empty = all)
- `allowedModels` — Array of model aliases this key can use (empty = all)
- `quotaName` — Name of assigned user quota (null = none)
- `comment` — Freeform description
- `traceEnabled` — Per-key debug capture state
- `traceEnabledGlobal` — Global debug state (affects all keys)

## traceEnabled vs traceEnabledGlobal

- `traceEnabledGlobal` — If false, no debug logs are captured for any key
- `traceEnabled` — Only matters if global is true; enables per-key capture

To capture debug for a limited key, **both** must be true. This two-tier
system allows admins to quickly disable all debugging without changing
per-key settings.

## Admin with keyName query

Admins can also view another key's identity by passing `?keyName=...`.
This returns the limited-shape response for that key.

post.summary: Rotate the current principal's key secret
post.description:
Generates a new `sk-…` secret and overwrites the key's `secret`
field. The plaintext value is returned exactly once.

## How it works

1. A new random secret is generated
2. The existing secret is replaced in the config
3. The new plaintext secret is returned **once** in the response
4. All requests using the old secret fail with 401

## Data retention

Historical usage data stays attached to the **key name**, not the secret
value. This means attribution history is preserved across rotations.

## Auditing

The old secret is immediately invalidated. If you need to audit who
had access, check the config commit history or logs.

## Admin usage

Admins must supply `?keyName=<name>` to rotate another user's key.
Limited callers always rotate their own key (the query param is ignored).

## Return value formatting

The new secret is returned as a string starting with `sk-`. Store it
securely — this is the only time it will be returned in plaintext.

parameters.name: keyName
parameters.description: Admin-only: specify which key to rotate. Limited callers always rotate their own key.

patch.summary: Update the current principal's key comment
patch.description:
Updates the freeform comment/description on a key.

## Usage

- Limited callers update their own key's comment
- Admins can update any key by passing `?keyName=<name>`

## Null vs empty string

- Setting `comment: null` removes the comment entirely
- Setting `comment: ""` (empty string) is also valid and stored as-is

There's no length limit enforced by the API (though the UI may truncate
display for very long values).

parameters.name: keyName
parameters.description: Admin-only: specify which key to update. Limited callers always update their own key.

post.summary: Enable or disable debug capture for the current principal's key
post.description:
Toggle debug capture for a specific API key. Used by limited principals
to enable debug for their own key, and by admins to set per-key debug
without affecting global settings.

## For limited principals

Enables debug capture for the key associated with the authenticated
principal. The principal must be limited (not admin).

## For admin principals

Admins can target any key using the `keyName` query parameter.
This is the **only** way limited users can toggle debug — they cannot
use PATCH `/v0/management/debug`.

## Response

Returns the new per-key state plus global state for context:
- `keyName` — The key that was modified
- `enabled` — Whether debug is now on for this key
- `enabledGlobal` — Current global debug state (for reference)

get.description:
Returns the quota status for the current key (or a specified key for admins).

## Why 200 with nulls?

Always returns 200 even when no quota is assigned. This is intentional —
the UI depends on a consistent 200 response to render the quota card
correctly (showing a "no quota" state vs an error state).

The response shape is:
- `key` — The key name
- `quotaName` — Name of assigned quota (null if none)
- `allowed` — Whether requests are currently allowed
- `currentUsage` — Current period usage (requests or tokens)
- `limit` — Period limit (null if no quota)
- `remaining` — Remaining in period (null if no quota)
- `resetsAt` — ISO timestamp when the period resets (null if no quota)
- `limitType` — `requests` or `tokens` (null if no quota)

## Admin with keyName query

Admins can view another key's quota by passing `?keyName=...`.

get.description:
Returns the full Plexus configuration object as JSON. This is the
same structure used by the database.

## JSON endpoints

- **This endpoint** — Returns the in-memory configuration as JSON
- **`GET /v0/management/config/export`** — Returns an export-friendly JSON object

Both contain nearly the same data; the export form omits derived runtime-only
fields and is suitable for backups or round-tripping through restore/import flows.

## What's included

- `providers` — All configured provider configs
- `models` — All model alias configs
- `keys` — All API key configs
- `mcp_servers` — All MCP server configs
- `user_quotas` — All user quota definitions
- `quotas` — Provider quota checker configs
- `system_settings` — Global system settings

**Admin only** — limited principals receive 403.

The endpoint uses adaptive bucketing to ensure meaningful visualizations:
- `hour` — returns hourly buckets for the last 24 hours
- `day` — returns daily buckets for the last 30 days
- `week` — returns weekly buckets for the last 12 weeks
- `month` — returns monthly buckets for the last 12 months

  based on the range duration

- **series** — Time-bucketed data, where each bucket contains aggregated
  counts and token sums
- **stats** — Fixed 7-day rolling window (always the last 7 days, regardless
  of `range`)

Dual-mode endpoint used by the dashboard to visualize request concurrency.

## Modes

### live (default)

Returns currently in-flight requests (where `durationMs IS NULL`),
grouped by provider and canonical model. Shows requests started within
the last hour. Useful for real-time dashboard monitoring.

### timeline

Returns bucketed historical counts over a time range, useful for
historical analysis. Groups by either `provider` or `model`.

## Parameters

- **mode** — `live` or `timeline`. Default: `live`.
- **timeRange** — For timeline mode: `hour`, `day`, `week`, `month`,
  or `custom`. Default: `hour`.
- **groupBy** — How to group: `provider` or `model`. Default: `provider`.
  Note: finer granularity (model) may produce more buckets; the adaptive
  algorithm caps at 100 buckets total.
- **startDate / endDate** — For custom time range (ISO timestamps).

## Adaptive bucketing

The endpoint auto-sizes buckets based on the time range to keep bucket
count between ~20-100 for readable charts. Smaller ranges = finer buckets.

## Scoping

Limited principals see only their own key's concurrency data.
Admins see all providers/models.

get.description:
Returns Prometheus metrics in text exposition format 0.0.4.

## Caching

Results are cached for `PLEXUS_METRICS_CACHE_TTL_MS` milliseconds
(default 15 seconds). The `X-Metrics-Cache` response header indicates:
- `HIT` — Response served from cache
- `MISS` — Fresh scrape performed

## Metric families (~40 total)

### Cumulative counters
- `plexus_requests_total` — Total inference requests by API type
- `plexus_tokens_total` — Total tokens processed (input/output/cached)
- `plexus_cost_total` — Total spend in dollars

### Today's metrics
- `plexus_requests_today` — Requests in current local day
- `plexus_tokens_today` — Tokens in current local day
- `plexus_cost_today` — Cost in current local day

### Per-provider metrics
- `plexus_provider_requests` — Requests per provider
- `plexus_provider_tokens` — Tokens per provider
- `plexus_provider_cost` — Cost per provider

### Per-model metrics
- `plexus_model_requests` — Requests per model alias
- `plexus_model_tokens` — Tokens per model alias

### Performance metrics
- `plexus_ttft_seconds` — Time to first token (histogram)
- `plexus_tp_seconds` — Tokens per second (histogram)

### Cooldown metrics
- `plexus_cooldown_active` — Currently in cooldown (gauge)
- `plexus_cooldown_seconds_remaining` — Seconds until cooldown expires

### In-flight metrics
- `plexus_in_flight` — Current requests being processed (gauge)

## Example scrape

```
# HELP plexus_requests_total Total requests
# TYPE plexus_requests_total counter
plexus_requests_total{api_type="chat"} 1234
plexus_requests_total{api_type="messages"} 567

# HELP plexus_cost_total Total cost in USD
# TYPE plexus_cost_total counter
plexus_cost_total 42.50
```

See `GRAFANA.md` at the repo root for PromQL examples.

get.description:
Returns all OAuth-capable providers that Plexus supports.

## Provider properties

- `id` — Unique identifier (e.g. `openai-codex`, `anthropic-claude-code`)
- `name` — Human-readable display name
- `usesCallbackServer` — Whether this provider uses the callback server
  for OAuth flow vs requiring manual code paste

## Callback vs manual code

- **usesCallbackServer: true** — Plexus runs a callback server that
  receives the OAuth redirect. The user visits the auth URL and is
  automatically redirected back. No manual copy-paste needed.

- **usesCallbackServer: false** — The provider returns an authorization
  code that must be manually pasted into Plexus. Use the
  `/sessions/{id}/manual-code` endpoint.

**Admin only** — limited principals receive 403.

post.summary: Start an OAuth onboarding session (admin only)
post.description:
Creates a new OAuth session to authenticate with a provider.

## providerId

The provider to authenticate with. Get the list from
`GET /v0/management/oauth/providers`.

## accountId

A user-chosen identifier for this account. This enables **multi-account
support** — you can have multiple credential sets for the same provider
with different account IDs. For example, you might have `personal` and
`work` accounts for the same provider.

The accountId becomes part of the credential storage key, so each
unique accountId gets its own credentials file.

## Response

Returns the new session with `status: waiting` and `authInfo.url`
populated. Poll `GET /v0/management/oauth/sessions/{id}` to track progress.

## Session lifecycle

```
waiting → prompt ↔ manual-code → complete
                ↘︎ failed
                ↘︎ cancelled
```

**Admin only** — limited principals receive 403.

accountId.description: User-chosen identifier for this account. Enables multi-account support per provider.

get.description:
Returns the current state of an OAuth session.

## Response fields

- `authInfo` — Populated when `status: waiting`. Contains the OAuth URL.
- `prompt` — Populated when `status: prompt`. Contains the provider's
  question/confirmation.
- `progress` — Array of status updates from the auth flow.
- `updatedAt` — Timestamp of the last update.

## Polling pattern

Poll this endpoint in a loop until `status` reaches `complete`,
`failed`, or `cancelled`.

## Session states

| State | Meaning | Next action |
|-------|---------|-------------|
| waiting | Auth URL ready | Open `authInfo.url` in browser |
| prompt | Provider needs confirmation | POST to `/prompt` |
| manual-code | Provider returns code manually | POST to `/manual-code` |
| complete | Credentials saved | Provider ready to use |
| failed | Auth error occurred | Check `progress` for error details |
| cancelled | User cancelled | Start new session |

**Admin only** — limited principals receive 403.

post.summary: Submit a prompt response (admin only)
post.description:
Submit a response to a provider's confirmation prompt.

## When to use

Use this when `GET /sessions/{id}` returns `status: prompt`. The session's
`prompt` field will contain the question or confirmation text.

## Request body

- `value` — The user's response (typically "yes" or "allow")

## Response

Returns the updated session. Poll again to check if authentication
succeeded (`status: complete`) or failed (`status: failed`).

**Admin only** — limited principals receive 403.

post.summary: Submit a manual authorization code (admin only)
post.description:
Submit an authorization code returned by the provider.

## When to use

Use this when `status: manual-code`. This is required for providers that
don't use the callback server (e.g. Codex CLI, Claude Code).

Some providers display a code on their website after authentication
that must be copied and submitted here. The code is typically a short
alphanumeric string.

## Request body

- `value` — The authorization code from the provider

## Response

Returns the updated session. Poll again to check if authentication
succeeded (`status: complete`) or failed (`status: failed`).

**Admin only** — limited principals receive 403.

The session status changes to `cancelled`. Any pending authentication

- User quit the auth flow
- Wrong account selected, need to start over
- Auth URL expired or is no longer valid

get.summary: List all provider quota checkers (admin only)
get.description:
Returns the latest quota snapshot for every configured provider.

## Path note

The path is `/v0/management/quotas` (not `/v0/quotas` as older documentation
may show).

## What this returns

A snapshot per provider, containing:
- Checker metadata (ID, type)
- OAuth account info (if using OAuth)
- Array of `Meter` readings, one per quota dimension the provider reports

## Which providers contribute data

Every provider with a `quota` configuration block has a
checker. The checker's `checkerType` matches the provider slug.

## Polling cadence

Quota checkers run on a scheduler (typically every 1–5 minutes). The
`meters` array shows the most recent reading for each meter. To
see historical data, use `/quotas/{checkerId}/history`.

**Admin only** — limited principals receive 403.

parameters.description: Checker ID in format `{provider}:{account}`, e.g. `naga:default`, `moonshot:work`. Use the checker IDs returned by `GET /quotas`.

get.summary: Latest quota for one checker (admin only)
get.description:
Returns the most recent quota sample for a specific provider/account
combination.

## Use case

Use this to get the current quota status for one provider without
fetching all checkers. Equivalent to filtering `GET /quotas` by
`checkerId`.

## Same shape as list endpoint

The response structure is identical to items in `GET /quotas` — a
`QuotaCheckerSnapshot` with the latest samples.

**Admin only** — limited principals receive 403.

Returns historical quota-snapshot rows for a specific checker, one row per
meter per check, sorted by `checkedAt` descending (most recent first).

## Query parameters

- **meterKey** — Filter to a single meter (e.g. `balance`, `five_hour`,
  `daily`). When omitted, returns rows for all meters the checker reports.
  Meter keys are provider-specific; discover them from the `meters[].key`
  field of a snapshot.

- **since** — Start of the time range. Supports two formats:
  - **Absolute**: ISO 8601 timestamp, e.g. `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`
  - **Relative**: `Nd` format, e.g. `7d` (last 7 days), `30d` (last 30 days)

## Response structure

- `checkerId` — The checker this history is for
- `meterKey` — The meter filter used (null if no filter)
- `since` — The timestamp of the earliest sample (null if no `since` filter)
- `history` — Array of `QuotaSample` snapshot rows

## Retention

Historical samples are retained for 30 days. Trying to query beyond
the retention window returns an empty array.

**Admin only** — limited principals receive 403.

parameters.description: Filter to a single meter (e.g. `balance`, `five_hour`, `daily`). Returns rows for all meters when omitted.

post.summary: Force an immediate quota check (admin only)
post.description:
Triggers an immediate quota check outside the normal scheduler cadence.

## Use case

Use this to get current quota data without waiting for the next scheduler
run. Useful after adding credits or changing provider configuration.

## What it does

- Immediately calls the provider's API to fetch fresh quota data
- Updates the local sample database
- Returns the checker's result (same shape as `GET /quotas/{checkerId}`)

## What it doesn't do

- **Does not bypass provider-side rate limits**. The check counts against
  any rate limits the provider imposes on quota API calls.
- **Does not modify the scheduler cadence**. The next scheduled check
  runs at its normal time.

**Admin only** — limited principals receive 403.

get.summary: List all user quota definitions (admin only)

Returns all user quota definitions keyed by name.

## Use case

Use this to see all available quota definitions and their current
configuration.

## Name regex

Quota definition names must match: `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-_]{1,62}$`
- Starts with lowercase letter or digit
- Allowed: lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, underscores
- 2–63 characters

**Admin only** — limited principals receive 403.

parameters.description: Quota definition name. Must match regex `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-_]{1,62}$` (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, underscores; 2–63 chars).

Returns a single quota definition by name.

put.description:
Creates a new quota definition or replaces an existing one.

## PUT vs PATCH

- **PUT** — Complete replacement. All required fields must be provided.
  Use for creating new definitions or full updates.
- **PATCH** — Partial update. Only provided fields are updated. Use
  for making small changes without sending the full definition.

## Validation

The request body is validated against the `UserQuotaDefinition` schema.

Partially updates a quota definition.

## PUT vs PATCH

- **PUT** — Complete replacement. All required fields must be provided.
- **PATCH** — Partial update. Only provided fields are updated. Only
  fields present in the request body are changed; missing fields retain
  their current values.

## Use cases

- Change just the limit: `{"limit": 50000}`
- Change just the duration: `{"duration": "2h"}`

**Admin only** — limited principals receive 403.

Deletes a quota definition.

## 409 Conflict

Returns 409 if any configured key still references this quota via its
`quota` field. You must either:
1. Remove the quota assignment from the key first
2. Delete the key itself

This prevents accidental deletion of quotas that are actively limiting
API keys.

**Admin only** — limited principals receive 403.

Resets usage counters for a key's quota to zero.

## What this does

- Sets the key's current usage to 0
- Resets any internal window tracking
- Does NOT delete or modify the quota definition itself

## What this doesn't do

- Does NOT remove the quota assignment from the key
- Does NOT affect other keys' usage

## Use cases

- Grant a "fresh start" to a key that hit its limit
- Reset after a billing cycle
- Clear accumulated usage before a new trial period

## Audit note

This operation is logged for audit purposes. The logs record which
admin performed the reset and when.

**Admin only** — limited principals receive 403.

Repairs a quota bucket by recomputing its usage from successful request
usage records instead of trusting the stored counter. The quota must be
attached to the key, directly or through the configured default quotas.

Rolling requests and rolling tokens quotas are rejected because their
decay history cannot be reconstructed exactly from request usage records.

**Admin only** — limited principals receive 403.

Returns the current quota enforcement status for a specific API key.

## Response shapes

Two possible shapes depending on whether a quota is assigned:

**Assigned (quota_name is set):**
```json
{
  "key": "acme_corp",
  "quota_name": "premium_hourly",
  "allowed": true,
  "current_usage": 45000,
  "limit": 100000,
  "remaining": 55000,
  "resets_at": "2026-02-19T01:00:00.000Z"
}
```

**Unassigned (quota_name is null):**
```json
{
  "key": "free_user",
  "quota_name": null,
  "allowed": true,
  "current_usage": 0,
  "limit": null,
  "remaining": null,
  "resets_at": null
}
```

## Why 200 for "no quota"

Returns 200 (not 404) even when no quota is assigned. This is intentional
— the UI needs to render a "no quota" state (unlimited) rather than an
error state. When `quota_name` is null, `allowed` is always `true` and
limit/remaining are null.

**Admin only** — limited principals receive 403.

post.summary: Synthetic test inference (admin only)
post.description:
Runs a canonical probe request directly against a (provider, model)
pair, bypassing alias resolution.

## Use case

Used by the admin UI's "test" button next to each alias target. Allows
testing a specific provider/model combination without going through
the normal routing pipeline. Internally shares the same probe machinery
as background exploration.

## Direct bypass

Unlike normal inference, this endpoint:
- Bypasses alias resolution — uses provider/model directly
- Uses only the provider's base URL and API key from config
- No retries, cooldowns, or quota checks applied
- Short timeout (typically 30s)

## Usage record attribution

Test requests appear in usage records with `apiKey = "probe"` and
`attribution = "manual"` (background exploration probes use
`attribution = "background"`). They are real requests that count
against provider quota.

## Response

Returns 200 with `success: false` for runtime errors (failed dispatch,
upstream errors). The UI needs to render error messages without
treating them as HTTP errors. Validation errors (missing fields,
unknown `apiType`, unsupported `transcriptions`) return 400.

## Request fields

- `provider` — Provider slug (e.g. `openai`, `anthropic`)
- `model` — Model name (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-3-opus`)
- `apiType` — API type (default: `chat`). Options: `chat`, `messages`,
  `gemini`, `responses`, `embeddings`, `images`, `speech`, `oauth`.
  The `transcriptions` API requires a file upload and is not supported
  by this endpoint.

**Admin only** — limited principals receive 403.

post.summary: Gracefully restart the process (admin only)
post.description:
Initiates a graceful shutdown and exits with status 0.

## Process manager assumption

This endpoint assumes a process manager is running (systemd, Docker,
PM2, etc.) that will automatically restart the Plexus binary after
exit.

## Behaviour

- `SIGTERM` is sent to initiate graceful shutdown
- Fastify stops accepting new connections
- In-flight requests are allowed to complete
- Server exits with code 0

## Alternative

For non-graceful restart, the process manager may be configured to
send `SIGKILL` after a timeout.

**Admin only** — limited principals receive 403.

  backup, migration, and cloning scenarios.

- **Full backup** (`?full=true`): Returns a gzipped tar archive (`.tar.gz`)
  containing a `manifest.json`, a `config.json` (same as config-only), and
  per-table `.csv.gz` files for operational/telemetry data (usage records,
  debug logs, errors, cooldowns, performance stats, quota snapshots, etc.).

Sensitive fields (API key secrets, OAuth tokens) are decrypted in the export
so the backup is portable across instances with different `ENCRYPTION_KEY` values.
Store the resulting file securely.

**Admin only** — limited principals receive 403.

post.summary: Restore database from a backup (admin only)
post.description:
Accepts a backup file and replaces all existing data in the database.

Two input formats are accepted:

- **`application/json`**: A config-only backup envelope (as produced by
  `GET /v0/management/backup` without `?full=true`). Restores configuration
  tables only; operational data is not affected.

- **`application/octet-stream`** / **`application/gzip`**: A gzipped tar archive
  (as produced by `GET /v0/management/backup?full=true`). Restores both
  configuration and operational data.

**Destructive operation** — all current data is deleted before the backup is
applied. For full archive restores, the entire operation runs in a single
database transaction; if any step fails, the database is rolled back to its
pre-restore state.

After a successful restore, a server restart is recommended so that in-memory
caches and long-lived connections pick up the new configuration.

**Admin only** — limited principals receive 403.

get.description:
Server-Sent Events stream of request lifecycle events, used by the
admin dashboard for real-time monitoring.

## Event types

- **started** — Request received, dispatched to provider.
- **updated** — Request metadata updated (e.g. token counts known).
- **completed** — Request finished (success or error). Contains the
  full `UsageRecord`.
- **created** — Legacy/alias for `started`.

Each event includes the `UsageRecord` payload (for `completed`) or
partial data (for `started`/`updated`).

## Ping

A `ping` event is sent every 10 seconds to keep the connection alive.

## Format

```
event: completed
data: {"requestId":"...","date":"...","provider":"openai",...}
id: 1735689599000
```

## Scoping

Limited principals see only events for their own API key.
Admins see all events.

Server-Sent Events stream of backend log entries emitted at or above the
current runtime log level.

## Event format

```
event: syslog
data: {"level": "info", "message": "Request started", "timestamp": "2024-01-01T12:00:00.000Z", ...}
```

## Event payload

Each `syslog` event contains:
- **level** — Log level: `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug`, `verbose`, or `silly`
- **message** — Log message text
- **timestamp** — ISO 8601 timestamp
- **context** — Additional fields (provider, model, requestId, etc.)

## Ping

A `ping` event is sent every 10 seconds to keep the connection alive.

## Level filtering

The stream honors the current runtime log level setting. Logs below
the current level are NOT emitted. Check `GET /v0/management/logging/level`
to see the current level. To receive all logs, ensure level is set to
`trace` or `debug`.

**Admin only** — limited principals receive 403.

get.description:
Returns the most recent backend log entries from Plexus's in-memory log ring buffer.

## Retention

Plexus keeps a bounded in-memory buffer of recent raw log objects. This endpoint
returns the newest entries first and does not persist logs across restarts.

## Query parameters

- `limit` — Maximum number of log entries to return (default 100, max 1000)
- `offset` — Number of newest entries to skip (default 0)

**Admin only** — limited principals receive 403.

post.summary: JSON-RPC message exchange
post.description:
Forwards JSON-RPC requests to a configured upstream MCP server.

## Header handling

- Client `Authorization` header is **stripped** — not forwarded
- Client `x-api-key` header is **stripped** — not forwarded
- Only the static `headers` from the server's config are forwarded
  to the upstream

## Response modes

- **JSON response** — Standard JSON-RPC response
- **Streamed (`text/event-stream`)** — Server-sent events for
  long-running operations

## Error codes

- `400` — Invalid server name (doesn't match regex)
- `404` — Server not found or disabled in config
- `502` — Upstream MCP server returned an error
- `504` — Upstream request timed out

**No auth** — MCP proxy endpoints are unauthenticated.

get.summary: SSE stream to the upstream MCP server
get.description:
Establishes a Server-Sent Events stream to the upstream MCP server.

## Use case

Some MCP servers use SSE for real-time event delivery. This endpoint
proxies that stream to the client.

## Query string passthrough

Any query parameters on the request are forwarded to the upstream
MCP server unchanged.

## Headers

- Upstream connection headers from the server's config are forwarded
- Client authentication headers are stripped

**No auth** — MCP proxy endpoints are unauthenticated.

delete.description:

## Use case

Cleanly closes the connection to the upstream MCP server. May trigger
cleanup handlers on the upstream.

**No auth** — MCP proxy endpoints are unauthenticated.

post.description:
The Plexus Management MCP server is an in-process Model Context Protocol
server exposing compact domain tools for managing Plexus.

## Authentication

Requires the `x-admin-key` header. Bearer inference keys are rejected.

## MCP disabled

When `mcpEnabled` is `false`, requests return HTTP 418
(`mcp_disabled`) before authentication. Enable it via
`PATCH /v0/management/config/mcp-enabled` or the MCP Servers UI.

## Transport

Uses the Streamable HTTP transport with JSON responses. Each request
creates a stateless per-request MCP server instance.

Options for the `web_search_coercion` provider adapter.
This adapter translates server-side web search tool entries to the format expected by the target provider, allowing clients to use any known web search tool format regardless of which provider Plexus routes to.
**Recognised incoming formats:**
- Anthropic: `{ "type": "web_search_20250305", "name": "web_search" }` - OpenAI: `{ "type": "web_search" }` - OpenRouter: `{ "type": "openrouter:web_search" }` - Google: `{ "googleSearch": {} }`
