pi_ai_model_id.description: Builtin pi-ai model ID used to resolve registry metadata for `auto_compat`. If omitted or not resolvable, auto-compat skips this model without failing the request.

enabled.description: Set to `false` to remove earlier instances of this adapter, including provider-level and implicitly injected ones. A later entry with `enabled: true` restores it.

adapter.description: Adapter name(s) applied to this specific model. Appended after any provider-level adapters. Accepts bare strings or `{ name, options }` objects for parameterized adapters (e.g. `model_override` with rules). See the provider-level `adapter` field for available values.

oneOf.description: Map of model ID → per-model configuration. Allows per-model pricing overrides and access aliases.

models.description: Models available on this provider. Either a simple list of IDs or a map of model ID → configuration for per-model pricing/type overrides.

headers.description: Static headers forwarded on every request to this provider. Useful for custom authentication schemes or provider-specific requirements.

maxConcurrency.description: Max concurrency across all models. Optional per-provider limit on how many requests can be in-flight simultaneously. Empty/null means no limit.

extraBody.description: Extra fields merged into every request body sent to this provider.

estimateTokens.description: When true, token counts are estimated locally rather than relying on the provider's response. Useful for providers that omit usage fields.

geminiThinkingEnabled.description: When true, enables Gemini-native thinking (extended reasoning) for this provider. Only applicable to Gemini-compatible providers.

auto_compat.description: When true, enables registry-aware compatibility mapping for all models under this provider that have a resolvable `pi_ai_model_id`. Plexus uses pi-ai builtin registry metadata to map client reasoning/thinking and generation intent to provider-specific request fields. The step is opt-in and skipped for models without a registry link.

pi_ai_provider.description: Builtin pi-ai provider ID used to validate `models[*].pi_ai_model_id` links and populate registry-backed model selectors. Custom pi-ai providers/models are not managed through Plexus; this field links only to pi-ai's builtin registry.

useClaudeMasking.description: When true, rewrites OpenAI-format requests to look like Claude requests before forwarding. Used for providers that require Anthropic-compatible request shapes.

quota_checker.description: Optional provider-level quota checker configuration. References a quota checker type from `GET /v0/management/quota-checker-types`.

model_autosync.description: Optional provider-level model discovery sync. When enabled, Plexus periodically fetches the provider's known model list and adds any missing models to this provider's `models` configuration without removing or overwriting existing model entries.

gpu_profile.description: Named GPU profile (e.g. `H100`, `A100`, `custom`). A display hint used by the frontend; the backend uses the four numeric fields below as the source of truth.

gpu_ram_gb.description: GPU RAM in GB. Used for energy estimation when combined with model_architecture.

gpu_bandwidth_tb_s.description: GPU memory bandwidth in TB/s. Used for energy estimation.

gpu_flops_tflop.description: GPU peak FLOPs in teraflops. Used for energy estimation.

gpu_power_draw_watts.description: GPU TDP in watts. Used for energy estimation.

enabled.description: Set to `false` to remove earlier instances of this adapter, including implicitly injected defaults. A later entry with `enabled: true` restores it.

adapter.description:
Adapter name(s) applied to every model under this provider. Adapters rewrite outbound request payloads (preDispatch) and inbound provider responses (postDispatch) to fix provider-specific field-name incompatibilities. Applied before model-level adapters.
Adapters can be specified as bare strings (backward compatible) or as objects with `{ name, options }` for adapters that require configuration.

 Available adapters:

- `reasoning_content` — Renames `reasoning`/`thinking.content` →
  `reasoning_content` on outbound assistant messages. Fixes Fireworks/
  DeepSeek providers that reject the `reasoning` field name.

- `suppress_developer_role` — Rewrites the `developer` role to `system`
  for providers that do not support the OpenAI `developer` role.

- `model_override` — Conditionally rewrites the provider model name
  based on request payload fields. Accepts a `rules` array in options
  where each rule specifies a `model` to match, a `rewriteTo` model name,
  and an array of `conditions` (OR semantics) using dotted field paths.
  Used for providers that expose reasoning variants as separate model
  names rather than respecting reasoning-related request fields.

- `reasoning_rewrite` — Declaratively rewrites reasoning/thinking fields
  in outbound request payloads. Different providers accept reasoning
  effort via different field names (e.g. `enable_thinking`, `thinking.type`,
  `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking`, `budget_tokens`, `thinking_budget`).
  This adapter maps from unified fields (e.g. `reasoning.enabled`,
  `reasoning.effort`) to provider-specific formats. Accepts a `rules`
  array in options where each rule specifies a `source` dotted path,
  an optional `when` condition (with `op` and `value`), an array of
  `rewrites` (each with `target` and `value`), and optional `strip`
  paths to remove after rewriting. This overlaps with registry-aware
  `auto_compat`; prefer `auto_compat` for models linked to the pi-ai
  builtin registry and keep manual rewrites as an explicit escape hatch.

- `web_search_coercion` — Translates server-side web search tool entries
  to the format expected by this provider. Clients may send any known web
  search tool format (`web_search_20250305`, `web_search`,
  `openrouter:web_search`, or `googleSearch`); the adapter rewrites it
  to the target provider's canonical shape. Accepts a `target` option
  (`"anthropic"`, `"openai"`, `"openrouter"`, or `"google"`) and an
  optional `max_uses` integer (Anthropic target only). Works transparently
  across all four incoming API surfaces (Chat Completions, Anthropic
  Messages, OpenAI Responses, and Gemini native).
  See [`WebSearchCoercionAdapterOptions`](#/components/schemas/WebSearchCoercionAdapterOptions).

- `normalize_anthropic_tool_ids` — Rewrites `tool_use` / `tool_result`
  identifiers that violate Anthropic's tool-id charset
  `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$` (e.g. Moonshot's `functions.WebSearch:3`), which
  Anthropic rejects with a hard HTTP 400. Injected automatically when the
  route's outbound wire format is Anthropic Messages AND the provider
  looks Anthropic (base URL containing `anthropic.com`, Anthropic OAuth,
  or Claude masking). Override per provider or model with
  `{ name: 'normalize_anthropic_tool_ids', options: {}, enabled: true }`
  to force it on for an Anthropic-compatible gateway hosted elsewhere, or
  `{ name: 'normalize_anthropic_tool_ids', enabled: false }` to opt out.

Adapters run on the outbound body whether or not the pass-through optimisation is active — a same-format request skips the transformer, but its body is still cloned, given the target model and the provider/model config fields, and run through the adapter chain before dispatch.

timeoutMs.description: Optional per-provider upstream request timeout in milliseconds. When omitted, Plexus uses the global timeout from `/v0/management/config/timeout`.

stallTtfbMs.description: Optional per-provider TTFB stall timeout override in milliseconds. Omit to inherit the global value. `null` disables TTFB stall detection for this provider.

stallTtfbBytes.description: Optional per-provider byte threshold used to confirm meaningful first output for stall detection. Omit to inherit the global value.

stallMinBps.description: Optional per-provider minimum throughput override in bytes per second. Omit to inherit the global value. `null` disables throughput stall detection for this provider.

stallWindowMs.description: Optional per-provider sliding-window width for throughput stall detection, in milliseconds. Omit to inherit the global value.

stallGracePeriodMs.description: Optional per-provider grace period before throughput stall detection starts, in milliseconds. Omit to inherit the global value.

MetadataOverrides.description: Override fields for model metadata. Used within alias `metadata` to override individual fields resolved automatically or sourced from an external catalog, or to provide all fields when `source` is `custom`.

name.description: Human-readable model name. Required when `metadata.source` is `custom` (no catalog fallback).

pricing.description: Per-token pricing strings (as reported by the provider catalog).

prompt.description: Cost per input token (as a decimal string, e.g. "0.000002").

input_cache_read.description: Cost per cached input token read.

input_cache_write.description: Cost per cached input token write.

input_modalities.description: Modalities this model accepts as input (e.g. `["text", "image"]`).

output_modalities.description: Modalities this model produces as output (e.g. `["text"]`).

supported_parameters.description: List of inference parameters this model supports (e.g. `["temperature", "top_p", "tools"]`).

context_length.description: Provider-reported maximum context length. Takes precedence over the top-level `context_length` override when both are set.

max_completion_tokens.description: Maximum output tokens the provider allows per request.

AliasConfig.description: Model alias configuration. Maps a client-facing model name to one or more provider targets, organised into ordered target groups. Stored in the database.

provider.description: Provider slug this target routes to.

model.description: Model ID to request from the provider.

enabled.description: When false, this target is skipped during dispatch.

target_groups.description: Ordered list of target groups. The dispatcher exhausts all healthy targets in group N before trying group N+1. At least one group is required.

type.description:
Model capability type — what the model produces. This is distinct from the wire protocol (which is configured via `preferred_api` or `access_via` on each provider model).
- **text** — Text generation (LLM). Supports all text wire protocols:
  chat completions, messages, gemini, responses, ollama.
- **embeddings** — Vector embeddings, including Gemini backends via
  automatic request/response transformation.
- **transcriptions** — Audio to text. - **speech** — Text to audio. - **image** — Image generation/editing.

priority.description:
Controls how selectors interact with API-type matching.
- **selector** — Apply each group's selector across its targets regardless of API type. - **api_match** — Filter targets to those whose provider supports the
  requested API type first, then apply the selector.

preferred_api.description: Advertised in /v1/models to inform clients of the recommended API surface for this alias. For text aliases, when omitted, Plexus infers `messages` for Anthropic/Claude models, `responses` for GPT models, `gemini` for Gemini models, and `chat_completions` for everything else. Non-text aliases do not receive an inferred value.

additional_aliases.description: Additional names this alias is known by. Requests using any of these names are routed identically to the primary slug.

use_image_fallthrough.description: When true, vision requests that fail image processing fall through to text-only handling rather than returning an error.

enforce_limits.description: When true, enforces the model's `max_tokens` / `max_output_tokens` constraint from metadata, rejecting requests that exceed it.

extraBody.description: Extra JSON body fields merged into every request dispatched through this alias. Merged after provider-level and model-level extraBody, so alias values win.

sticky_session.description: When enabled, multi-turn conversations prefer the same provider/model from the previous turn (when still healthy) for better prompt-cache hit rates.

metadata.description: Model metadata strategy. When omitted or set to `auto`, Plexus derives a canonical identity from the alias targets, looks for an exact catalog entry, and falls back to conservative name and modality heuristics. Catalog sources pin a specific entry, `custom` supplies all fields, and `disabled` suppresses enrichment. Overrides win over resolved values.

source_path.description: Optional label. Not used for any catalog lookup.

overrides.description: All metadata lives here for custom sources. `name` is required because there is no catalog fallback.

model_architecture.description: Model architecture details used for inference energy estimation. When modified, triggers async recalculation of kWh for all affected historical usage records.

input_price_per_million.description: Shorthand simple pricing: input price per million tokens. Equivalent to setting `pricing` to `{ source: "simple", input: <value>, output: <output_price_per_million> }`. Only used when `pricing` is not set.

output_price_per_million.description: Shorthand simple pricing: output price per million tokens. See `input_price_per_million`.

pi_model.description: Link to a pi-ai model to include its compatibility options as `pi_options` in `GET /v1/models`.

pricing.description: Advanced pricing configuration. Takes precedence over `input_price_per_million` / `output_price_per_million` when set.

slug.description: OpenRouter model slug to pull live pricing from.

amount.description: Flat fee charged per request regardless of token count.

advanced.description: List of model behaviour modifiers applied during request/response transformation.

KeyConfig.description: API key configuration. Controls access to Plexus inference endpoints. Stored in the database.

secret.description: The API key secret. Stored encrypted at rest. Format is typically `sk-...` but any string is accepted.

comment.description: Freeform description or notes about this key. Max 500 characters.

expiresInMinutes.description: Optional lifetime for a new key, expressed as positive whole minutes. This value is accepted only when creating the key and cannot be changed.

expiresAt.description: Absolute expiry time as Unix epoch milliseconds.

disabledAt.description: Time the key was disabled as Unix epoch milliseconds.

allowedProviders.description: Restrict this key to specific providers only. If empty, the key can be used with any provider.

excludedProviders.description: Optional denylist. If set, routing will not use these provider IDs.

excludedModels.description: Optional denylist. If set, this key cannot use these model aliases.

allowedModels.description: Restrict this key to specific model aliases only. If empty, the key can be used with any model.

allowRawPassthrough.description: Privileged provider-wide raw access. Existing provider allow/deny lists still apply; model restrictions do not apply to raw requests.

quota.description: Name of a user quota definition to enforce. If null, no quota is enforced for this key.

UserQuotaDefinition.description: User quota definition. Defines a rate limit that can be assigned to API keys. The quota enforcement middleware checks keys against their assigned quota definition and rejects requests that would exceed the limit.

type.description:
Quota window type.
- **rolling** — Sliding window of `duration` length (e.g. `1h`, `30m`,
  `1d`). Requires the `duration` field.
- **daily** — Resets at midnight local time each day. - **weekly** — 7-day rolling window starting from first request. - **monthly** — Calendar month window starting from first request.

limitType.description:
What the quota tracks and counts against the limit.
- **requests** — Number of inference requests. Each API call counts as 1. - **tokens** — Sum of all token fields: `tokensInput` + `tokensOutput`
  + `tokensCached` + `tokensCacheWrite`. This is the total tokens
  processed, not just input or output.
- **cost** — Accumulated cost in USD based on the model's pricing
  configuration.

limit.description:
Maximum allowed value within the window. Unit depends on `limitType`:
- For `requests`: number of requests - For `tokens`: number of tokens - For `cost`: cost in USD

duration.description: Window length for `type: rolling`. Format: number + unit. Examples: `1h` (1 hour), `30m` (30 minutes), `1d` (1 day), `5h` (5 hours). Required when `type` is `rolling`, ignored otherwise.

Config.description: Full in-memory Plexus configuration. This is the authoritative reference for all runtime settings, stored in the database.

providers.description: Map of provider slug to provider configuration.

models.description: Map of model alias slug to alias configuration.

keys.description: Map of API key name to key configuration.

mcp_servers.description: Map of MCP server name to server configuration.

user_quotas.description: Map of quota definition name to quota configuration.

quotas.description: Array of provider quota checker configurations.

system_settings.description: Global system settings and feature flags.

CompactionSettings.description: Context compaction settings. All fields are optional overrides.

error.description: Fixed error type indicating validation failure.

details.description:
Array of validation issues. Each item is a Zod validation error object describing a specific field failure.
Common fields in each detail object: - `path` — Array of keys leading to the invalid field (e.g. `['body', 'model']`) - `message` — Human-readable description of the failure - `code` — Zod error code (e.g. 'invalid_type', 'invalid_enum_value') - `expected` — Expected type or value - `received` — Actual type or value received

MeterStatus.description:
Utilisation severity level for a quota meter.
- **ok** — 0–75% utilisation. Healthy, plenty of quota remaining. - **warning** — 75–90% utilisation. Approaching exhaustion. - **critical** — 90–100% utilisation. Near exhaustion, take action soon. - **exhausted** — 100% utilisation. Quota fully consumed, requests will fail.

Meter.description:
A single quota meter reading for one provider checker, as returned in the `meters` array of a quota snapshot. Mirrors the `Meter` type in `packages/backend/src/types/meter.ts`.

A checker reports one meter per quota dimension it tracks (e.g. a balance meter and/or one or more time-windowed allowance meters). Meters are identified by `key`, not by a fixed window-type enum.

key.description: Stable identifier for this meter within the checker. Examples: `balance`, `five_hour`, `daily`. Provider-specific; there is no fixed global enum. Used as the `meterKey` filter on the history endpoint.

label.description: Human-readable label for the meter (e.g. `Five-hour window`).

group.description: Optional grouping label for multi-tenant or sub-account setups.

scope.description: Optional scope qualifier for the meter.

kind.description:
What the meter tracks.
- **balance** — A prepaid account balance (unit typically `usd`).
  Renders as a wallet in the UI.
- **allowance** — A time-windowed rate limit (unit `requests`, `tokens`,
  or `percentage`). Renders as a progress bar in the UI.

unit.description: Unit of measurement. Common values: `usd`, `requests`, `tokens`, `percentage`; providers may define additional units.

limit.description: Maximum allowed value for this meter. Null when unbounded/unknown.

used.description: Amount consumed so far. Null when unbounded/unknown.

remaining.description: Calculated as `limit - used`. May be negative. Null when unbounded/unknown.

utilizationPercent.description:
Utilisation of the meter. Either a numeric percentage, or a sentinel:
- **unknown** — The provider did not report enough information to compute utilisation. - **not_applicable** — Utilisation is not meaningful for this meter (e.g. a balance with no limit).

periodValue.description: Length of the allowance window (only for `kind: allowance`). e.g. `1` for a 1-hour window. Null for `kind: balance`.

periodUnit.description: Unit for `periodValue` (only for `kind: allowance`). Null for `kind: balance`.

periodCycle.description:
How the allowance window resets (only for `kind: allowance`).
- **fixed** — Resets at a calendar boundary (e.g. midnight). - **rolling** — Sliding window from first use. Null for `kind: balance`.

resetsAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp when the meter window resets. Null for rolling windows or balances without a defined reset time.

exhaustionThreshold.description: Optional utilisation percentage at which the checker gates the provider onto cooldown.

UsageRecord.description: Per-request usage record stored in `request_usage`. Populated after each inference request completes (or errors). Fields may be null on error paths.

startTime.description: Request start timestamp in epoch milliseconds.

apiKey.description: API key used for authentication (may be hashed depending on config).

attribution.description: Attribution label from API key suffix (e.g. `sk-xxx:copilot` → "copilot"). Null if no suffix was provided.

incomingApiType.description:
API format received from the client.
- **chat** — OpenAI Chat Completions (`/v1/chat/completions`). - **messages** — Anthropic Messages (`/v1/messages`). - **responses** — OpenAI Responses API (`/v1/responses`). - **gemini** — Google Gemini (`/v1beta/models/*`). - **embeddings** — OpenAI Embeddings (`/v1/embeddings`). - **transcriptions** — OpenAI Audio Transcriptions (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`). - **speech** — OpenAI Audio Speech (`/v1/audio/speech`). - **images** — OpenAI Images (`/v1/images/*`). - **oauth** — OAuth-authenticated provider session.

provider.description: Final provider used for the request (e.g. "openai", "anthropic").

attemptCount.description: Number of request attempts (including retries). 1 = no retries.

retryHistory.description: JSON-encoded retry chain array. Each entry contains provider, model, error info, and whether it was the final attempt. Null if no retries occurred.

incomingModelAlias.description: Model alias as specified in the request (before resolution).

canonicalModelName.description: Resolved canonical model name. For aliases with `model_architecture`, this is the target; otherwise same as `incomingModelAlias`.

selectedModelName.description: Final model name sent to the upstream provider. May differ from `canonicalModelName` due to provider-specific transformations.

finalAttemptProvider.description: Provider used for the final (successful or last) attempt.

finalAttemptModel.description: Model used for the final attempt.

allAttemptedProviders.description: JSON array of all providers attempted during this request (each appears once, in order of attempt). Null if only one provider was used.

outgoingApiType.description: API format sent to upstream provider. May differ from `incomingApiType` due to protocol transformation.

tokensInput.description: Number of input tokens consumed. Reported by provider when available; otherwise estimated based on character count. Null on error.

tokensOutput.description: Number of output tokens generated. Null on error.

tokensReasoning.description: Number of reasoning/thinking tokens (for models that report them separately, e.g. o1, o3, Claude Opus). Null if not applicable or on error.

tokensCached.description: Number of tokens served from prompt cache. Only populated when cache was hit. Null otherwise.

tokensCacheWrite.description: Number of new tokens written to cache. Null if caching was not enabled or not applicable to the request.

tokensEstimated.description: Flag indicating token count source. 0 = actual usage from provider; 1 = estimated from character counts when provider did not report.

costInput.description: Cost in dollars for input tokens.

costOutput.description: Cost in dollars for output tokens.

costCached.description: Cost in dollars for cached tokens (typically discounted).

costCacheWrite.description: Cost in dollars for tokens written to cache.

costTotal.description: Total cost in dollars (sum of all cost fields).

costSource.description:
Pricing method used to calculate cost fields.
- **default** — No pricing configured; all cost fields are zero. - **simple** — Per-token pricing from `input_price_per_million` /
  `output_price_per_million` on the model.
- **openrouter** — Pricing fetched from OpenRouter at request time. - **defined** — Explicit pricing ranges from `pricing.range` in model
  config.
- **per_request** — Flat fee per call; full amount in `costInput`,
  others zero.
- **null** — Cost source not yet resolved; record is still in-flight
  or pricing information was unavailable at recording time.

costMetadata.description: JSON-encoded pricing details including rate, currency, and any provider-specific pricing overrides used.

durationMs.description: Total request duration in milliseconds (from start to final response received). Null if request was abandoned early.

ttftMs.description: Time to first token in milliseconds. Only populated for streaming requests. Null for non-streaming or if first token timing unavailable.

tokensPerSec.description: Output tokens per second (throughput). Calculated as `tokensOutput / (durationMs - ttftMs)` for streaming requests. Null for non-streaming or if calculation invalid.

kwhUsed.description: Estimated energy consumption in kilowatt-hours. Calculated from `model_architecture` token estimates and provider-specific energy coefficients. Requires `model_architecture` to be set on the alias.

isPassthrough.description: Whether the request was a direct passthrough (no transformation).

isRaw.description: Whether the request used the provider-wide raw proxy.

requestMethod.description: Original HTTP method for raw requests.

requestPath.description: Raw provider path suffix and query string.

responseStatus.description:
Outcome of the request. Raw upstream failures may be represented as `HTTP <status>` so the provider's exact status remains visible.
- **success** — Upstream returned a successful response. - **error** — Upstream returned an error or the request failed. - **pending** — Request is in-flight (used for async tracking). - **cancelled** — The downstream client disconnected and Plexus cancelled the upstream request. - **timeout** — Plexus aborted the upstream request because it exceeded the configured timeout. - **stall** — Plexus aborted the request because stream stall detection fired.

toolsDefined.description: Number of tools/function definitions in the request.

messageCount.description: Number of messages in the conversation (including system).

parallelToolCallsEnabled.description: Whether parallel tool calls were enabled in the request.

toolCallsCount.description: Number of tool calls made in the response.

finishReason.description: Model's finish reason (e.g. "stop", "length", "tool_calls"). Null if not applicable or on error.

hasDebug.description: Whether debug logs exist for this request (mirrors presence in `debug_logs` table).

hasError.description: Whether error records exist for this request (mirrors presence in `inference_errors` table).

UsageSummary.description: Aggregated usage statistics over time windows.

range.description: Time range for series data. Format depends on query param (e.g. "24h", "7d", custom start/end). Affects only the series field.

bucketStartMs.description: Start of the time bucket (epoch ms).

requests.description: Number of requests in this bucket.

inputTokens.description: Sum of input tokens across all requests.

outputTokens.description: Sum of output tokens across all requests.

cachedTokens.description: Sum of cached tokens across all requests.

cacheWriteTokens.description: Sum of cache-write tokens across all requests.

kwhUsed.description: Sum of energy usage (kWh) across all requests.

tokens.description: Total token count = inputTokens + outputTokens + cachedTokens + cacheWriteTokens.

totalTokens.description: Total tokens (input + output + cached + cacheWrite) in the window.

totalKwhUsed.description: Total energy usage in the window.

totalDurationMs.description: Sum of all request durations in milliseconds.

today.description: Aggregation since local midnight (time-of-day based, not UTC).

totalCost.description: Total cost in dollars since midnight.

DebugLog.description: Debug capture for an inference request. Can contain request/response snapshots at various transformation stages. Only populated if debug is enabled for the request (via header or key configuration).

requestId.description: The request this debug log belongs to.

rawRequest.description: Original client request body as received by Plexus, before any transformation. This is what the client sent.

transformedRequest.description: Request body after Plexus transformation, as sent to the upstream provider. Includes any protocol conversion (OpenAI → Anthropic, etc.).

rawResponse.description: Raw response from the upstream provider, before Plexus transformation. May include provider-specific fields not in the standard schema.

transformedResponse.description: Response after Plexus transformation, as returned to the client. This is what the client received.

rawResponseSnapshot.description: Snapshot of the raw response taken at completion. Stored for reference even if the original stream was consumed.

transformedResponseSnapshot.description: Snapshot of the transformed response at completion. Mirrors what was sent to the client for non-streaming requests.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the debug log was created (epoch ms).

McpUsageRecord.description: MCP proxy usage record. Tracks each request through the MCP server proxy.

server_name.description: Name of the MCP server this request was proxied to.

upstream_url.description: Full URL of the upstream MCP server endpoint.

method.description:
HTTP method used for the MCP proxy request.
- **GET** — Opens an SSE stream for server-to-client notifications. - **POST** — Sends a JSON-RPC message exchange (initialize, tool calls,
  etc.).
- **DELETE** — Terminates an upstream MCP session.

jsonrpc_method.description: The JSON-RPC method name for POST requests (e.g. "tools/list", "tools/call", "resources/read"). Null for GET requests.

tool_name.description: Name of the tool being called (for tool/* methods). Null if the request was not a tool call (e.g. resources/read, prompts/list).

api_key.description: API key used for proxy authentication.

attribution.description: Attribution label from API key suffix.

has_debug.description: Whether debug logs exist for this request.

error_code.description: Error code if the request failed (e.g. -32600, -32601).

error_message.description: Error message if the request failed.

Cooldown.description: Provider cooldown entry indicating a provider/model pair is temporarily unavailable due to consecutive failures.

model.description: Model name or alias that is in cooldown.

expiry.description: Absolute cooldown expiration timestamp in epoch milliseconds. After this time, the provider/model can be retried.

timeRemainingMs.description: Derived time remaining until expiry (expiry - currentTime). Useful for UI display. 0 if already expired.

consecutiveFailures.description: Number of consecutive failures that triggered this cooldown. Resets to 0 on any successful request.

PerformanceRow.description: Aggregated performance metrics for a provider/model pair. Sample window is typically 24 hours. Error responses and failed streaming requests are excluded from sample_count but counted in failure_count.

avg_ttft_ms.description: Average time to first token in milliseconds.

min_ttft_ms.description: Minimum time to first token observed.

max_ttft_ms.description: Maximum time to first token observed.

avg_tokens_per_sec.description: Average post-TTFT throughput in tokens/sec (output tokens / streaming time).

avg_e2e_tokens_per_sec.description: Average end-to-end throughput in tokens/sec (output tokens / total request time).

sample_count.description: Number of successful requests in the sample window. Excludes errors and failed streaming requests.

success_count.description: Number of requests that returned successfully.

failure_count.description: Number of requests that failed (any error status).

last_updated.description: Timestamp of last metric update (epoch ms).

modules.description: List of module names to include in console output.  An empty array means all modules are shown.

providerId.description: Provider identifier (e.g. `openai-codex`, `anthropic-claude-code`). Matches a provider from `/v0/management/oauth/providers`.

accountId.description: User-chosen identifier for this account. Enables multi-account support — you can have multiple credential sets for the same provider with different account IDs.

status.description:
Session lifecycle state.
- **waiting** — Session created; the user should open the auth URL from
  `authInfo.url`.
- **prompt** — Provider requires a user confirmation (e.g. typing
  "yes"). Submit via the `prompt` endpoint.
- **manual-code** — Provider requires a manually pasted authorization
  code (Codex CLI, Claude Code). Submit via the `manual-code` endpoint.
- **complete** — Credentials stored on disk, provider ready. - **failed** — Authentication error occurred. - **cancelled** — User cancelled the session.

authInfo.description: Authorization URL and instructions. Populated when status is `waiting`. Contains `url` (the OAuth consent page) and optionally `instructions` (human-readable guidance).

url.description: The OAuth consent URL the user must visit.

prompt.description: Prompt response from the provider. Populated when status is `prompt` — contains the question or confirmation the user must answer.

progress.description: Array of status updates/messages from the auth flow. Useful for debugging and showing progress to the user.

createdAt.description: Unix timestamp (ms) when the session was created.

updatedAt.description: Unix timestamp (ms) when the session was last updated.

QuotaCheckerSnapshot.description:
Latest quota snapshot for a single provider checker, returned by `GET /v0/management/quotas` and `GET /v0/management/quotas/{checkerId}`.

A checker reports its current readings as an array of `Meter` objects (one per quota dimension). When the last check failed, `success` is false, `meters` is empty, and `error` carries the failure message.

checkerId.description: Unique identifier for this quota checker. Format: `{provider}:{account}`, e.g. `naga:default`, `moonshot:work`.

checkerType.description: Checker type identifier (e.g. `naga`, `moonshot`, `openai-codex`). Maps to the provider quota-checker definition.

oauthAccountId.description: OAuth account identifier. Present when the provider uses OAuth authentication. Used to distinguish multiple accounts for the same provider.

oauthProvider.description: OAuth provider identifier (e.g. `openai-codex`, `anthropic-claude-code`). Present when credentials are stored via OAuth flow.

success.description: Whether the most recent quota check succeeded.

error.description: Error message when the most recent check failed. Omitted on success.

meters.description: Current meter readings for this checker (one `Meter` per quota dimension). Empty when the last check failed.

QuotaSample.description:
A single persisted quota-snapshot row, as returned in the `history` array of `GET /v0/management/quotas/{checkerId}/history`.

These are raw rows from the `meter_snapshots` table (one row per meter per check), so field names follow the stored column shape (camelCased by the ORM). For the current/latest reading of a meter, see the `Meter` schema — `getLatestQuota` maps these rows into the friendlier `Meter` shape. There is no `windowType` field; a meter is identified by `meterKey`.

id.description: Database record ID for this snapshot row.

checkerId.description: Foreign key to the checker this snapshot belongs to. Matches `QuotaCheckerSnapshot.checkerId`.

checkerType.description: Checker type identifier at capture time.

meterKey.description: Stable identifier for the meter this row captures (e.g. `balance`, `five_hour`, `daily`). Provider-specific; used as the `meterKey` query filter on the history endpoint.

kind.description: Whether this meter tracks a prepaid balance or a time-windowed allowance.

unit.description: Unit of measurement. Common values: `usd`, `requests`, `tokens`, `percentage`; providers may define additional units.

group.description: Optional grouping label for multi-tenant or sub-account setups.

limit.description: Maximum allowed value for this meter. For `balance` kind, the prepaid balance in dollars. For `allowance` kind, the request/token limit.

used.description: Amount consumed so far. Null when unbounded/unknown.

remaining.description: Calculated as `limit - used`. May be negative.

utilizationState.description:
Whether a meaningful utilisation was reported for this row.
- **reported** — `utilizationPercent` holds a numeric percentage. - **unknown** — The provider did not report enough to compute utilisation. - **not_applicable** — Utilisation is not meaningful for this meter.

utilizationPercent.description: Percentage of quota consumed (`(used / limit) * 100`). Only meaningful when `utilizationState` is `reported`; null otherwise.

periodValue.description: Length of the allowance window. Null for `balance` kind.

periodCycle.description: How the allowance window resets. Null for `balance` kind.

resetsAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp when the meter window resets. Null for rolling windows or balances without a defined reset time.

success.description: Whether the quota query to the provider succeeded. False if the provider API was unreachable or returned an error.

checkedAt.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was captured.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when this record was persisted. Usually matches `checkedAt`.

QuotaStatus.description: Quota enforcement status for an API key. Returned by the status check endpoint; used by the quota middleware to decide whether to allow or block requests.

key.description: The API key name this status applies to.

quota_name.description: Name of the quota definition assigned to this key. Null when no quota is assigned — requests are allowed without rate limiting.

allowed.description: Whether requests are currently allowed. False when the user has exceeded their quota limit. The quota middleware blocks requests when this is false and returns 429.

current_usage.description: Current usage count/tokens within the quota window. What this represents depends on `limitType` in the quota definition (tokens or requests).

limit.description: Maximum allowed usage for the quota window. Null when no quota is assigned (unlimited).

remaining.description: Calculated as `limit - current_usage`. Null when no quota is assigned. Can be negative if over-consumption occurred.

resets_at.description: Timestamp when the quota window resets and usage counters clear. Null for rolling windows or when no quota is assigned.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the backup was created.

dialect.description: Source database dialect (informational; not used on import).

providers.description: Map of provider slug to provider configuration.

models.description: Map of model alias slug to model configuration.

keys.description: Map of key name to API key configuration.

user_quotas.description: Map of quota name to quota definition.

mcp_servers.description: Map of MCP server name to server configuration.

settings.description: Map of setting key to value.

QuotaExceeded.description:
Returned when a user's quota limit is exceeded. The request is rejected
with HTTP 429.

## When this is returned

This response is returned by inference endpoints (`/v1/*`) when:
1. The API key has an assigned quota (via `keys[*].quota` in config)
2. The key's usage has reached or exceeded the quota limit
3. The quota enforcement middleware blocks the request

## Response fields

- `error.type` — Always `quota_exceeded`
- `error.message` — Human-readable error message
- `error.quota_name` — Name of the quota definition being enforced
- `error.current_usage` — Usage at the time of rejection
- `error.limit` — The limit that was exceeded
- `error.resets_at` — When the quota window resets (if applicable)

## Rate limiting behaviour

After this response is returned, subsequent requests continue to be
blocked until:
- The quota window resets (e.g., midnight for daily, window expiry for rolling)
- An admin clears the quota counters via `POST /v0/management/quota/clear`
- The quota assignment is removed from the key

error.message: Quota exceeded: premium_hourly limit of 100000 reached

ProviderError.description:
Upstream provider returned an error or the dispatcher exhausted retries.

## When this is returned

This response is returned by inference endpoints (`/v1/*`) when:
1. The upstream provider returns a 5xx error (server error)
2. Network failure occurs while calling the provider
3. The dispatcher exhausts all retry attempts

## Response semantics

The response uses the `OpenAIError` schema but with specific type values:
- `type: server_error` — Provider returned 5xx
- `type: api_error` — Network or connection error

## Fields that survive

When a request fails after multiple provider retries, the `routing_context`
field in the error contains metadata about the retry chain:
- `providers_attempted` — Array of provider slugs that were tried
- `last_provider` — The final provider that failed
- `attempt_count` — Number of providers attempted
- `errors` — Array of error messages from each attempt (if available)

## Example

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "All providers failed: last error: 503 Service Unavailable",
    "type": "server_error",
    "code": 503,
    "routing_context": {
      "providers_attempted": ["openai", "anthropic", "cerebras"],
      "last_provider": "cerebras",
      "attempt_count": 3
    }
  }
}
```

## Affected endpoints

- `POST /v1/chat/completions`
- `POST /v1/messages`
- `POST /v1/responses`
- `POST /v1/codex/responses`
- `POST /v1/embeddings`
- `POST /v1/audio/transcriptions`
- `POST /v1/audio/speech`
- `POST /v1/images/generations`
- `POST /v1/images/edits`

AdminAuthError.description:
Missing or invalid admin key.

Returned when:
- Request to an admin-only endpoint has no `x-admin-key` header
- The provided admin key is invalid or doesn't match the configured key

Limited principals (non-admin) trying to access admin endpoints receive
a 403 `forbidden` error via the standard `AuthError` response, not this one.
